scenes.caption: 261 BCE — The Mauryan Empire
scenes.text: Ashoka rules the largest empire the subcontinent has ever seen. Only one kingdom on the eastern coast refuses to bow: Kalinga.

scenes.caption: The Invasion Begins
scenes.text: Ashoka marches south with an enormous army. Kalinga, though smaller, resists fiercely — every village arms itself.

scenes.caption: The Battlefield
scenes.text: The two armies clash near the Daya River. The fighting is brutal and prolonged, unlike anything Ashoka has faced before.

scenes.caption: Victory, and Its Price
scenes.text: Mauryan forces prevail. But the cost is staggering — over 100,000 are reported dead, and the river is said to run red.

scenes.caption: The Emperor Walks the Field
scenes.text: Ashoka tours the aftermath himself. The scale of suffering — soldiers and civilians alike — shakes him to his core.

scenes.caption: A Transformation
scenes.text: Haunted by what he has done, Ashoka turns toward the teachings of the Buddha, renouncing further conquest by force.

scenes.caption: The Edicts
scenes.text: He has his new philosophy carved into rock and pillar across the empire — proclamations of non-violence, tolerance, and welfare.

scenes.caption: Legacy
scenes.text: The Kalinga War becomes the hinge point of Ashoka's reign — one of history's starkest examples of a conqueror remaking himself.

scenes.caption: 1757 — Bengal on the Brink
scenes.text: The young Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah rules Bengal, wary of the growing power of the British East India Company.

scenes.caption: A Web of Betrayal
scenes.text: Robert Clive secretly conspires with Mir Jafar, the Nawab's own commander, promising him the throne in exchange for treachery.

scenes.caption: The Battlefield at Plassey
scenes.text: On a rain-soaked field, Siraj's much larger army faces Clive's modest force — but Mir Jafar's troops barely fight at all.

scenes.caption: Collapse
scenes.text: Without his strongest general's support, Siraj's army disintegrates. He flees the field as defeat becomes inevitable.

scenes.caption: A New Nawab, A New Master
scenes.text: Mir Jafar is installed as a puppet ruler. But real power now lies with the East India Company, not the Nawab's court.

scenes.caption: The Turning Point
scenes.text: Plassey hands the Company control of Bengal's treasury and trade — the first domino in two centuries of British rule.

scenes.caption: Legacy
scenes.text: What began as a trading company's local intrigue becomes the seed of an empire that will govern the subcontinent until 1947.

scenes.caption: 1942 — A World at War
scenes.text: As Japan advances through Southeast Asia, Britain refuses to commit to Indian self-rule despite the war's demands on India.

scenes.caption: Gandhi's Ultimatum
scenes.text: On 8 August, the Congress passes the Quit India resolution — demanding an immediate end to British rule.

scenes.caption: "Do or Die"
scenes.text: Gandhi addresses the nation in Bombay, urging every Indian to resist non-violently — and to act as if already free.

scenes.caption: Mass Arrests
scenes.text: Within hours, the British arrest Gandhi, Nehru, and the entire Congress leadership, hoping to decapitate the movement.

scenes.caption: The Nation Responds Anyway
scenes.text: Without its leaders, ordinary Indians take charge — strikes, protests, and underground networks erupt nationwide.

scenes.caption: Brutal Suppression
scenes.text: Tens of thousands are arrested; some areas see British forces respond with extreme force, including aerial strafing of crowds.

scenes.caption: Legacy
scenes.text: Though crushed in the short term, Quit India proves Britain can no longer govern India by consent — independence is now inevitable.

scenes.caption: 1761 — Maratha Ambition
scenes.text: The Maratha Confederacy has expanded across most of India, openly challenging what remains of Mughal authority.

scenes.caption: An Afghan Invader
scenes.text: Ahmad Shah Abdali marches from Afghanistan, allying with regional powers wary of Maratha dominance.

scenes.caption: The Armies Gather at Panipat
scenes.text: Two massive forces converge on the same field that saw Babur's and Akbar's decisive battles centuries before.

scenes.caption: A Long Siege of Attrition
scenes.text: For months the armies face off, Maratha supply lines strained as Abdali's forces cut off their resources.

scenes.caption: The Battle Itself
scenes.text: When battle finally comes, exhausted and starved Maratha forces are decisively defeated, suffering catastrophic losses.

scenes.caption: Aftermath
scenes.text: Tens of thousands of Maratha soldiers and camp followers die. The Confederacy's momentum is shattered for a generation.

scenes.caption: Legacy
scenes.text: The power vacuum left by this defeat opens the door wider for British expansion across the subcontinent in the decades that follow.
